decisions.reason: Locates index.js inject ["apiProxy"] and ctx.apiProxy.llm.providers() with line citation, maps to DSH-0.1.2-A1-01, explains the llm.providers → llm/listProviders migration (correctly identifying host-plane ctx.llm injection per the field note), and flags the dead @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency in package.json as deleted in alpha.1. All essential elements present with correct reasoning.

All six remaining categories are accounted for with hit/no-hit conclusions and scan evidence (no patch declaration, no events, no filesystem access, no commands/contributes, no server/WebSocket, no spawn). session-notes.js is correctly characterized as a pure string/array utility with the filename being only historical naming, and cordis.patch.yml is handled correctly — the 'no patch file/declaration' wording under the source-patch category is acceptable per the rubric since the composition file is in scan scope and not misclassified as host-source modification.

Explicitly states zero hits in the six categories only means 'not found in current patterns', not proof of compatibility; notes scan coverage limits (dependency-graph resolution, the still-present dead apiproxy dependency) and that static scanning cannot replace real execution. The decisive #3 apiProxy break is clearly distinguished from the six negative categories.

Specifies post-migration build/typecheck, an isolated 0.1.2-alpha.2 profile cold boot confirming no pending, and a real llm.listProviders() provider call, framed as mandatory steps after migration rather than as executed checks.
